Read gridded soil drainage class from HWSD onto WHEP's grid.

Source: R/soil_ph.R
read_soil_drainage.Rd

Reads the drainage class of HWSD (Harmonized World Soil Database) version 1.2 and returns, for each 0.5-degree cell, the class most of its native HWSD pixels fall in, named as the drainage classes of image_gnm_leaching_factors (Table 2 of Beusen et al. 2015), the soil drainage factor of the IMAGE-GNM root-zone denitrification. HWSD drainage is a reference condition on flat terrain (0-0.5% slope), not a measured water table. Soil drainage is a static HWSD property: the result has no year column.

Usage

read_soil_drainage(
  hwsd_dir = NULL,
  data = list(),
  source = c("auto", "pin", "local"),
  version = NULL,
  example = FALSE
)

Source

FAO/IIASA/ISRIC/ISSCAS/JRC (2012). Harmonized World Soil Database version 1.2. FAO, Rome and IIASA, Laxenburg. Drainage classes: the field DRAINAGE and its lookup D_DRAINAGE in HWSD.mdb; documentation p. 10 (drainage classes after FAO 1995, flat terrain). Class names: Beusen, A. H. W. et al. (2015). Geosci. Model Dev. 8, 4045-4067, Table 2.

Arguments

hwsd_dir

Path to the directory holding hwsd_data.csv and hwsd.bil. Defaults to Sys.getenv("WHEP_HWSD_DIR"). Supplying it derives the grid locally rather than reading the pin.

data

Optional named list of pre-loaded inputs: cell_polity (lon, lat, at minimum), used to crop the HWSD raster and a pinned grid to the region of interest, and drainage_counts, a per-class pixel count grid that replaces both routes.

source

Where the grid comes from. "auto" (default) reads the published pin unless hwsd_dir is given; "pin" always reads it; "local" always derives it from an HWSD archive. The pin is preferred so that every user shares one vintage: HWSD exists in two incompatible versions (v1.2 topsoil 0-30 cm, HWSD2 D1 0-20 cm) and the carbon balance reports 0-30 cm.

version

Pin version, passed to whep_read_file(). NULL takes the version frozen in whep_inputs.

example

If TRUE, return a small fixture instead of reading data. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A tibble with lon, lat, soil_drainage_class (one of "very_poorly_drained", "poorly_drained", "imperfectly_drained", "moderately_well_drained", "well_drained", "somewhat_excessively_drained", "excessively_drained") and method_soil_drainage.

Details

Each HWSD map unit takes the drainage class with the largest summed share over its soil components, and each 0.5-degree cell the class with the most pixels. Ties go to the wetter class (the lower HWSD code), and a tied cell is marked in method_soil_drainage. The published pin holds the per-class pixel counts, not the class, as the pin of read_soil_hydraulic() does.

The HWSD v1.2 codes map as follows, each read from the database's own D_DRAINAGE lookup (the documentation gives the basis of the classes, p. 10, but not the codes): 1 Very Poor to very poorly drained, 2 Poor to poorly drained, 3 Imperfectly to imperfectly drained, 4 Moderately Well to moderately well drained, 5 Well to well drained, 6 Somewhat Excessive to somewhat excessively drained and 7 Excessive to excessively drained. No HWSD v1.2 soil unit carries code 7. A code outside 1-7 aborts, and so does an extract that is not HWSD v1.2, whose coding differs.

Cells whose HWSD units carry no drainage class (open water, ice and other non-soil units) are absent from the result. They are not gap-filled, because carrying a neighbour's class there would be a method choice.

Caching

Aggregating the HWSD raster to the 0.5-degree grid takes about an hour per pass, and its result depends only on the archive and the target grid, so it is cached under rappdirs::user_cache_dir("whep"). The cache key covers the archive's raster and header (size and modification time), the resolution, the requested columns, the target grid's cells and the derived map-unit values, plus an algorithm version that is bumped whenever a change would move the numbers. Set WHEP_HWSD_CACHE_DIR to relocate it.

Examples

read_soil_drainage(example = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>     lon   lat soil_drainage_class method_soil_drainage   
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <chr>               <chr>                  
#> 1 -0.25 -0.25 well_drained        hwsd_v1.2_drainage_code
